Independent finite-grid code passed; it is not used to justify continuum claims.

value.rationale: The alternating two-radius triangular superlattice is a physical and geometric design appearing in a 2005 optical paper. A complete four-branch coverage phase curve and strict balancing law for heterogeneous disk size is a natural geometric covering optimization, not a substitution of a prior square-checkerboard or index-three triangular formula. The equal-radius triangular optimum is known, but no single-color radius theorem alone decides the competing two-size thresholds or proves the strict cost bound.
